body:
Kathmandu. The government is preparing to establish an 'Infrastructure Development Fund' with an authorized capital of Rs 100 billion with the objective of increasing investment in infrastructure development.

The government is establishing such a fund to amend the legal provisions related to infrastructure development according to the federal system of governance, to mobilize alternative financial resources, and to expand long-term investment in urban infrastructure.

The Ministry of Infrastructure Development has clarified that 'the fund is proposed to end the situation of relying solely on the traditional budget to raise the large investment required in infrastructure'. In addition to the funds received from the government and various levels of government, the fund will be able to obtain loans and grants from domestic and foreign donor agencies.

For this, 1 billion ordinary shares will be arranged. The capital structure has been prepared to include investment from the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, local levels, government institutions, banks and financial institutions, and international financial institutions in the fund. According to the proposed structure, the Government of Nepal will have a 40 percent share and provincial governments will have a 5 percent share in the fund.

Similarly, metropolitan cities, sub-metropolitan cities, and municipalities have been proposed to have a 15 percent share, and rural municipalities have a 10 percent share. The remaining shares include a 15 percent share for government corporations, funds, institutions, banks, and international financial institutions, and a 15 percent share for private sector banks and financial institutions, as per the draft.

The main objective of establishing this fund is to reduce the compulsion of relying solely on the traditional government budget to raise the large investment required in the infrastructure sector. To achieve the economic development goals set by the Sixteenth Plan, significant capital will be required, and the government plans to mobilize alternative financial resources such as foreign investment, public-private partnership, mixed investment, and green and climate finance.

Furthermore, the fund will also be given the authority to raise necessary capital by issuing debentures and other debt instruments. It is expected that this will end the situation of waiting for government grants or annual budgets for infrastructure projects and ensure long-term financial resources.

The proposed fund will be able to mobilize financial instruments based on shares, debentures, bonds, and guarantees in infrastructure projects. The draft also includes provisions for providing loans or grants for projects selected in partnership between federal, provincial, and local levels. The responsibility of providing economic and technical consulting services for the identification, feasibility study, construction, and operation of projects proposed by provincial and local levels will also be given to the fund.

This will not only provide funds for project construction but also assist in project preparation, financial structuring, and operation. The bill places special emphasis on expanding the financial resource mobilization capacity of local levels. The fund can provide guarantees for the security of debt instruments issued by local levels.

In addition, provisions have been made to provide loan guarantees, partial loan guarantees, payment guarantees, and liquidity guarantees. However, providing guarantees will not automatically mean that all projects will receive loans. The final financial decision will be made based on project feasibility, revenue sources, debt repayment capacity, and risk assessment.

To systematize loan repayment, the draft also includes a proposal for the fund to operate a loan repayment reserve fund and account. Similarly, provisions have been made to issue green bonds and sustainable infrastructure bonds to increase investment in environmentally friendly and sustainable infrastructure. This will help attract investment in projects related to climate change mitigation, environmental protection, and sustainable urban development.

A 10-member steering committee will be formed to operate and manage the fund, chaired by the Secretary of the Ministry of Infrastructure Development or a designated person. The committee will include representatives from various ministries, provincial and local levels, subject matter experts, and representatives from private sector banks and financial institutions.

The draft proposes the appointment of a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for a term of four years based on open competition to manage the daily operations of the institution. This is expected to establish professional expertise and performance-based leadership in the institution's management.

Considering the financial stability and risk management of the fund, a strict provision has been proposed whereby only after depositing 20 percent of the net profit into a reserve fund each year can dividends be distributed to shareholders. The draft mentions a provision for the final audit of the institution's income and expenditure to be carried out by the Auditor General or a designated auditor.
